data.long_meaning: Ashvitha is the name of the goddess of horses in Hindu mythology. She is often depicted riding a horse and is believed to bring prosperity and good luck. The name Ashvitha is derived from the Sanskrit word 'ashva', which means 'horse'. The name Ashvitha carries the meaning “Horse Goddess” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ashvitha usually hope their child will grow to embody horse goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of strength and grace, associated with the divine horse goddess.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ashvitha total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_sanskrit.name: आश्विथा
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The name Ashvitha is derived from the Sanskrit words 'ashva' meaning horse and 'itha' meaning abode or residence. It can be interpreted as 'abode of the horse' or 'warrior maiden'. In Hindu mythology, horses represent power, strength, and courage. Therefore, the name Ashvitha signifies a strong and powerful woman.
